newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Feelgood shoppers to boost Kingfisher.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Feelgood shoppers to boost Kingfisher.

text.p: Half-year results from retail group Kingfisher Plc next Wednesday are set to benefit from signs the feel-good factor is be making a comeback in Britain.
Analysts predict Kingfisher's pre-tax profits will romp ahead driven by a surge in consumer demand plus benefits from management efforts to improve the group's performance.
Pretax profits are forecast to come in between 97 and 115 million stg, against 74.6 million stg last time. The dividend is set to rise to about 4.9 pence from 4.5 pence, analysts said.

Even Kingfisher's home decorating business B&Q, which had a disastrous profit slump in the past financial year is expected to revive. An upturn in the housing market and consumer spending generally is set to boost B&Q's operating profits to about 40 million stg from 31.8 million, they said.
B&Q could see like for like sales rise by about four percent.
"One can only think the improvement in the housing market and the general improvement in consumer spending is going to kick in," said one retail analyst who asked to remain anonymous.

Electricals retailer Comet, while not doing as well as rival Dixons Group Plc, is expected to reduce its 8.7 million stg loss last year to around a two million loss, according to another analyst, who also declined to be identified.

Woolworths is set to be back in profit after a 900,000 stg loss last time and produce like for like sales growth of around seven to eight percent. But analysts said they did not give much weight to first half figures as the homewares chain makes most of its money at Christmas.
Superdrug is expected to raise profits slightly from last year's 15 million stg, helped by a change in product mix, analysts said.

Darty, Kingfisher's French electricals business, is forecast to make profits of about 46 million stg up from 40 million, but analysts say the chain has had a tough time because of the sluggish French market.
A strong set of figures could boost the shares and push up full year profit forecasts, analysts said. But there are already some questions about how much longer the good news can last, said one.
